# Security Policy

Toj is a messenger. Reports that affect the confidentiality, integrity or
availability of user communication are taken seriously and are reviewed by a
maintainer directly.

## Supported versions

Toj has not been publicly released. There is no supported shipped version, and
no user data is at risk from this repository today.

| Version | Supported |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | Yes — this is the development target |
| Tagged pre-releases | No |

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Please do not open a public issue, pull request or discussion for a security
problem.** A public report is readable by everyone the moment it is filed.

Use either channel:

1. **GitHub private vulnerability reporting** — open the repository's
   [Security tab](https://github.com/mmarufov/Toj/security/advisories/new) and
   submit a draft advisory. This is the preferred route; it keeps the report,
   the discussion and the eventual fix in one private thread.
2. **Email** — <support@tojchat.tech> with `SECURITY` in the subject line.

A useful report includes what an attacker can do, the steps or code path that
gets them there, and the commit you tested against. A proof of concept helps but
is not required — a precise description of the flaw is worth more than a
half-working exploit.

## What to expect

- **Acknowledgement within 5 days.** Toj is maintained by a small team; if you
  have not heard back in that window, send a follow-up.
- An assessment of severity and an intended fix window, shared with you directly.
- Credit in the release notes when a fix ships, unless you would rather not be
  named.

## Scope

**In scope** — anything in this repository: the iOS client, the backend in
`server/`, the build and verification scripts, the CI workflows, and the
deployment templates in `infra/`.

**Out of scope** — the marketing site at `tojchat.tech`, findings that require a
physically compromised or jailbroken device, denial of service by brute
resource exhaustion, and reports generated by an automated scanner with no
demonstrated impact.

## Handling test data

Do not use real people's phone numbers, messages or accounts to demonstrate a
finding. If a report necessarily contains personal data, say so and we will
arrange a channel for it.
